name: lstat
synopsis: int lstat(const char *restrict pathname, struct stat *restrict statbuf);
description: The lstat() function retrieves information about a file specified by pathname and stores it in the provided buffer. It is identical to stat(), but if pathname is a symbolic link, it returns information about the link itself rather than the file it refers to. No permissions are required on the file, but execute permission is needed on the directories in the path.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Pathname of the file or symbolic link to retrieve information about.

parameters.name: statbuf
parameters.description: Pointer to a struct stat buffer where the file status information is stored.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Search permission is denied for one of the directories in the path prefix of pathname.
Too many symbolic links encountered while traversing the path.
A component of pathname does not exist or is a dangling symbolic link.
A component of the path prefix of pathname is not a directory.
pathname refers to a file whose size, inode number, or number of blocks cannot be represented.

bugs: Fields in the stat structure may contain state information from different moments during execution, potentially leading to inconsistencies if the file is modified concurrently.
